stem:
Esha holds two cardboard corner pieces. The diagram shows angle $R$ and angle $S$ drawn from those corners.

Which claim correctly decides which angle is larger by overlaying?

options.text: Match the vertices and align one arm of each; the free arm of angle $R$ opens farther, so angle $R$ is larger.
Leave the vertices apart on the desk and judge the openings from separate places.
Knowing that angle $R$ is larger is what creates the overlay of the cardboard corners.
Any two cardboard corner pieces must be equal angles.

teacher.key_rationale: Overlaying requires coinciding vertices and one aligned arm; the free arm then shows R is larger. Judging with vertices apart omits that condition. Saying knowledge of size creates the overlay reverses the relation. Treating every cardboard corner as equal over-extends the comparison rule.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as two cardboard corner angles R (wider) and S (narrower) for overlay comparison.
